title: docs: clarify static browser PKCE clients
author: q8paradise
pr_body_excerpt:
## Summary

- Clarifies that PKCE-enabled static/public browser clients can exchange the authorization code directly, instead of implying every integration needs a server.
- Adds a browser `fetch` example that validates `state`, requires the saved verifier, removes callback parameters, discovers the token endpoint, and reuses the exact registered redirect URI.
- Documents memory-first/session-only token handling and warns against `localStorage`, URLs, analytics, and logs.
- Links both server-backed and browser-only in-repo references.

## Verification

- Confirmed discovery advertises S256 and token authentication method `none`; the live token endpoint's CORS preflight allows browser POSTs.
- Checked `enter.pollinations.ai/src/routes/oauth.ts`, `src/routes/well-known.ts`, `src/index.ts`, `apps/oauth-client-demo`, and `apps/oauth-test`.
- Checked all open PR file overlaps; none covers this static-client guidance.
- Ran `git diff --check`, Node syntax validation for the new snippet, Markdown fence/link checks, directory checks, and an added-line secret scan. No packages, builds, or test suites were run.

## Security

The example fails closed on missing/mismatched state or verifier, removes transient OAuth data, and avoids persistent/callback-URL token exposure.

gist.headline: Browsers can bring their own pollen
gist.blurb: Static browser apps can now follow a clearly marked PKCE trail from authorization code to token, no server-shaped scarecrow required. The guide also keeps those fresh tokens out of URLs, logs, and the localStorage compost heap.
gist.summary: Updated BRING_YOUR_OWN_POLLEN.md with a browser-only PKCE flow showing direct authorization-code exchange via fetch, state and verifier validation, OIDC token-endpoint discovery, and the exact registered redirect URI.
gist.impact: Developers building static public browser clients now have a secure in-repo reference for exchanging codes directly while keeping tokens memory-first or session-only instead of exposing them in localStorage, callback URLs, analytics, or logs.
